title: Stadium Sledding Shenanigans
description: Haul snow up to the football stadium stands, build yourselves a run, and sled off the bleachers until one of you wipes out laughing.

title: Ice Block Hill Racing
description: Grab a block of ice from the store, find the longest grassy hill around, and take turns riding it down. Cheap, chaotic, and faster than you'd think.

title: Snow Court Tennis
description: Clear off a court, or just play straight through the drifts, and find out what a rally looks like when the ball dies in six inches of powder.

title: Tubes Now, Hot Lunch Later
description: Spend the morning flying down the tubing hill until your legs give out, then thaw out over a hot lunch the two of you definitely earned.

title: Parking Lot Snowman Prank
description: Sneak out and build a full-size snowman dead center in the institute parking lot, then find a spot nearby to watch people try to drive around it.

title: Snowman Build-Off, Cocoa Prize
description: Challenge another couple to a snowman-building contest, judge each other's work without mercy, then warm up with hot chocolate or spiced cider by the fireplace.

title: Snow Sculptures Holding Hands
description: Sculpt his-and-hers snow versions of yourselves holding hands, flop down for snow angels, settle things with a snowball fight, and finish with hot tea.

title: Snow Fort Siege
description: Each of you builds a fort worth defending, then declare war. Stockpile your snowballs first, because whoever runs out of ammo first loses the whole yard.

title: Snow Tag, Then Chili
description: Chase each other around outside until you're both soaked and out of breath, then head in for something hot: chili, soup, sloppy joes, cocoa, whatever's easiest.

title: Spray-Paint the Snow
description: Fill squirt guns or spray bottles with food-colored water, then use a fresh snowfall as your canvas for designs, doodles, and messages to each other.

title: Initials in a Fresh Lot
description: Find an untouched parking lot after a snowfall and plow your feet through it, stomping out your two initials with a plus sign between them.

title: Sledding in Sunday Best
description: Put on the clothes you'd normally save for a nice dinner, then go sledding in them anyway. The photos are worth whatever the dry cleaner charges.

title: Backyard Cold War
description: Pick your ammo, snowballs if it's winter and water balloons if it isn't, set a boundary line, and go to war until you're both soaked and laughing.

title: Squirt Gun Ambush After Dark
description: Fill up a couple of squirt guns, kill the porch light, and hunt each other through the dark yard. Wear something you don't mind soaking through.

title: Croquet in the Cold
description: Set up a croquet course out in the snow, or play it at night with flashlights on the wickets, and enjoy a game built for absolutely none of this.

title: Glow Stick Snowball Fight
description: Wait until midnight, tape glow sticks to yourselves and pack a few into snowballs, then battle in the dark where all you see are streaks of light.

title: Igloo Sleepover
description: Spend the afternoon packing and stacking snow blocks into a real igloo, then haul in sleeping bags and spend the whole night inside the thing you built.

title: Backward Sledding Obstacle Course
description: Set up an obstacle course down the hill, then run it sitting backward on your sleds. Steering blind is the entire point, so count crashes and crown a winner.

title: Snow Portraits, Face to Face
description: Pack up two mounds of snow and carve each other's portraits into them. The likenesses will be unflattering, the photos will be great, and nobody really wins.

title: Steepest Hill, Fanciest Outfit
description: Dress like you're headed somewhere expensive, find the steepest hill in town, and sled it anyway. Formal wear was not designed for this, which is the point.

title: Dress the Snowman Contest
description: Raid your closets for the worst clothes you own, build a snowman each, and dress them to win. Find someone neutral to judge, or just argue about it.

title: Picnic in the Powder
description: Hike out into the snow with a lunch packed, stomp yourselves a flat spot, and eat it right there in the middle of all that white and quiet.

title: Race the Snow Maze
description: Stomp a maze into a big field of fresh snow, then time each other running it. Keep adding dead ends until one of you gets genuinely turned around.

title: Snow Ice Cream, Two Spoons
description: Scoop a big bowl of clean fresh snow, stir in condensed milk and vanilla, and eat the fastest dessert you'll ever make before it melts on you.

title: Midnight Snowshoe Under Stars
description: Strap on snowshoes and head out around midnight. The snow throws starlight back at you, the trail is completely empty, and the quiet out there is unreal.

title: A Castle Made of Snow
description: Take on something ambitious: a snow castle with more than one room, walls tall enough to stand behind, and a doorway the two of you can actually fit through.

title: The Sledding Music Video
description: Pick a dramatic song, sled the same hill from every camera angle you can manage, then cut it together into the music video absolutely nobody asked for.

title: Snowman Family Drama
description: Build a whole family of snowmen, then give each one a name, a job, and a backstory. By the third snowman, the family feud writes itself.

title: Cafeteria Tray Sledding
description: Borrow a couple of trays from the dining hall, find the slickest hill nearby, and learn that a flat sheet of plastic beats most real sleds.

title: Snowflake Catching Championship
description: Stand out in the falling snow with your heads tipped back and count how many flakes each of you catches on your tongue. Loser makes the cocoa.

title: Sketchbooks in the Snow
description: Hike out to a view you both like, pull out a couple of cheap sketchbooks, and draw the same snowy landscape. Comparing them afterward is the best part.

title: Sleeping Bag Sledding
description: Climb into sleeping bags at the top of a slope and slide down like a pair of oversized caterpillars. Steering is impossible, which is exactly the fun.

title: Snow Slip-N-Slide
description: Find a steep hill, pack the snow into a long slick chute, and take turns launching yourselves down it. Wear layers you don't mind soaking through.

title: Snow Forts, Water Balloons
description: Build two snow forts, then load up with water balloons instead of snowballs. Save this one for a warmer winter day unless you're feeling brave.

title: Headlamps and Hot Cocoa
description: Hit the sledding hill after dark with headlamps strapped on and thermoses of hot cocoa waiting at the top. Every run feels twice as steep at night.

title: The Giant Snow Spiral
description: Walk a huge spiral into an untouched snowfield, then follow it all the way to the center together. Find high ground afterward to see how it turned out.

title: Hold Hands All the Way Down
description: Sit on separate sleds at the top of the hill, grab each other's hand, and see if you can make it to the bottom without letting go.

title: Wipeout Blooper Reel
description: Sled the hill with a camera rolling and keep every crash, faceplant, and runaway sled. Cut the worst ones together into a blooper reel that night.

title: Freezer Ice Sculpting
description: Freeze water in bowls and pans overnight, then carve the blocks with whatever tools you've got. Work fast, keep towels handy, and expect a puddle.

title: Snow Angel Design Contest
description: Flop into fresh snow and see who can make the most creative angel out of it, wings and halos and all. Standing back up without wrecking it is the hard part.

title: Sled by Phone Flashlight
description: Head to the hill after sunset with nothing but your phone flashlights, and take turns lighting the run for each other on the way down.

title: Snowball Bowling Alley
description: Pack a flat lane into the snow, shape ten snow pins at the far end, and roll snowballs down it until one of you finally bowls a strike.

title: Sledding Through History
description: Pick a couple of historical figures, dress the part as best your closets allow, and sled the hill in full costume. Staying in character all the way down is mandatory.

title: Hunt the Perfect Snow Shot
description: Hike the snowy trail with one mission: find the single best photo spot out there. Take turns being the photographer and the one freezing for the shot.

title: Snow Bench at Sunset
description: Carve a bench out of packed snow facing west, sit down together with something warm in hand, and stay put until the sun drops behind the hills.

title: Footprint Art in Fresh Snow
description: Pick a pattern, a heart or your initials or a long spiral, and walk it into untouched snow. Find higher ground afterward to see how it came out.

title: Bubbles That Freeze Mid-Air
description: Wait for a properly subzero morning, blow soap bubbles outside, and watch them freeze into delicate crystal spheres. Try catching one before it shatters on you.

title: Rainbow Icicles
description: Snap off a few hanging icicles, drip food coloring down them until they streak like stained glass, then photograph the results in the afternoon sunlight.

title: Compass, Map, Buried Treasure
description: Navigate a snowy landscape with nothing but a compass and a hand-drawn map, hunting down hidden markers one by one. Put a clock on it to raise the stakes.

title: Blindfolded Sled, Trusted Voice
description: One of you sleds blindfolded while the other calls out steering from the top of a gentle slope, then you swap. It takes more trust than you'd expect.

title: Riddles in the Woods
description: Hide riddles and small prizes along a snowy trail that lead to a cozy cabin, with a sweet note waiting inside for whoever gets there first. End with hot cocoa.

title: Hot Spring Soak and Chicken Fight
description: Find a hot spring and sink in until you're both loose and pink from the heat. Bonus points for an extremely undignified chicken fight in the shallow end.

title: Two Paddles, One Canoe
description: Rent a canoe, and a trailer if you need one, then pick a calm stretch of water and find out how well the two of you actually paddle in sync.

title: Lakeside Camp Stove Cooking
description: Haul a camp stove or a small grill down to the lake and cook a real meal out there, whether that's breakfast, lunch, or dinner by the water.

title: Scuba in the Shallow End
description: Sign up for an intro scuba session at a public pool and get your first taste of breathing underwater, with no ocean and no nerves required.

title: Water Skis and a Cookout
description: Round up a group, take turns getting dragged across the lake behind the boat, and finish the day with a cookout on shore while everyone dries off.

title: Slow Dance in the Deep End
description: Put music on by the pool, wade in together, and dance in chest-deep water where every move is slow and nobody can see your terrible footwork.

title: Kayak Lessons at BYU-I
description: Take a kayaking session in the pool at BYU-I, where the water is warm, an instructor is right there, and tipping over is part of the lesson.

title: Sunrise Yoga on a Paddleboard
description: Paddle out onto flat early-morning water and work through a few yoga poses on your boards as the sun comes up. Dress for a swim, because you'll take one.

title: Slip-N-Slide Into Home
description: Set up a whiffle ball diamond with kiddie pools for first and second base and a slip-n-slide running into home. Sliding in soaked is not optional.

title: All Day at the Water Park
description: Spend a whole day working through the slides, the wave pool, and the lazy river, and don't leave until you've each ridden your favorite one twice.

title: Soap Boat Regatta
description: Carve little boats out of bars of soap, then race them down the canal and see whose design stays upright longest before it dissolves into suds.

title: Jaws, Watched From a Raft
description: Float a raft in the pool, set up a screen poolside, and watch Jaws from the water. You'll both flinch at least once, which is the entire point.

title: Car Wash Water Fight
description: Wash each other's cars in the driveway, let the hose fight break out the way it inevitably does, and reward yourselves with lunch once everything's clean.

title: Sunrise Swim and Breakfast
description: Get to a quiet private lake before the sun is fully up, take a bracing swim to wake yourselves up, and eat breakfast on the shore with nobody else around.

title: Paddleboard Picnic in a Cove
description: Rent a pair of paddleboards, paddle out to a secluded cove, and eat lunch floating right there. A dry bag for the food is your friend here.

title: Splash Pad After Hours
description: Find a splash pad in the evening once the kids have cleared out, run through the jets in the clothes you showed up in, and be eight years old again.

title: Pool Noodle Jousting Tournament
description: Get a few friends together, hand everyone a pool noodle, and joust it out in the water until only one pair is still upright and undefeated.

title: Naval Battle, Water Gun Class
description: Take two boats out on the lake, load up the biggest water guns you can find, and fight it out on open water until somebody finally surrenders.

title: Snorkel a Hot Spring
description: Bring masks to a natural hot spring and actually look at what's down there. The water stays warm enough that neither of you will want to get out.

title: Backyard Slip-N-Slide Gauntlet
description: String together slip-n-slides, sprinklers, and whatever else the yard offers into one soaking obstacle course, then time each other running the whole thing.

title: Hunt for Hidden Coves
description: Rent a small motorboat for a few hours and go looking for the coves nobody else bothers with. Pack a lunch and stop wherever the water looks best.

title: Rock Dams and Cold Swims
description: Wade into a shallow river and stack rocks into a dam that actually holds water, cooling off with a swim every time you finish another section.

title: Synchronized Swimming, Your Song
description: Pick a song you both love, choreograph a genuinely ridiculous synchronized swimming routine to it, and perform the whole thing for an audience of nobody.

title: Tube Float With a Cooler
description: Drop a couple of tubes into a calm river, tie a cooler to one of them, and let the current carry you both downstream all afternoon.

title: Midnight Waves
description: Hit a wave pool during a late-night session and swim the swell together. It's quieter, warmer, and far more romantic than the same place at 2pm.

title: Beginner's Luck at the Lake
description: Head out to a lake with a couple of rods and see what bites. No experience needed, and catching absolutely nothing is a perfectly good outcome.

title: Jet Ski Race to Dinner
description: Rent jet skis, race each other across the water to a beach, and have dinner there once you've both stopped shaking from the ride over.

title: Floating Water Balloon Piñata
description: Hang water balloons over the pool, take turns swinging at them blindfolded from a floatie, and accept that you'll both get soaked either way.

title: Rope Swing Into the Deep
description: Find a natural swimming hole with a rope swing, take turns launching off it, and spend the afternoon daring each other up to the higher branch.

title: Floatie Relay Chaos
description: Set up an obstacle course across the pool, then race it on inflatable floaties. Steering one of those things in a straight line is nearly impossible.

title: Swim a Slot Canyon
description: Hike into a slot canyon and swim the pools between the walls, with cold water below and towering rock on both sides. Check that the water is safe first.

title: Pontoon Stargazing Cruise
description: Rent a pontoon boat for the evening, motor out until the shore lights fade, then cut the engine and lie back on the deck to watch the stars come out.

title: Water Park, No Lines
description: Hit a splash zone water park during off-peak hours when the lines are short, then ride everything as many times as your legs will let you.

title: Garden Hose Obstacle Course
description: Take a few hoses and sprinklers to a park, rig up the most elaborate soaking obstacle course you can manage, and race each other through it.

title: Synchronized Dock Diving
description: Take turns launching off a dock in matched pairs, scoring each other on form, splash size, and general commitment to a very silly bit.

title: Nature's Hot Tub, Open Late
description: Find a natural hot tub of a spring, sink in once it's dark, and stay put until you're both pruned and the stars are all the way out.

title: Canoe Tour, Camera Stops
description: Rent a pair of canoes and paddle a scenic stretch of river, pulling over to the bank whenever a view is too good not to photograph.

title: Hunting Heart-Shaped Rocks
description: Wade up a shallow creek with your shoes in hand, hunting for rocks shaped like hearts. Whoever finds the best one has to give it away.

title: Glowing Pool Party
description: Throw a pool party after dark with floating LED lights bobbing across the surface. The whole backyard turns a strange, wonderful color once the sun is down.

title: Snorkel Scavenger Hunt
description: Write a list of things to find on the lake bottom, pull on snorkels, and race to check off the most before you run out of breath.

title: The Cooler Is the Raft
description: Load a big cooler with lunch, push it out onto the water as your floating table, and eat while you tread water beside it.

title: Dive for Coins, Buy Ice Cream
Tea Party on the Pool Floor
Picnic at Stuart Falls
description: Take the water tank trail in Provo up to Stuart Falls, then spread out a picnic somewhere you can eat with the waterfall right in front of you.

title: Hike Now, Rope Swing Later
description: Hike out to a local rope swing spot, then cool off launching yourselves into the water below. Bring a towel and something dry for the walk back.

title: Skipping Stones Showdown
description: Hike out to a lake or stream, then settle in on the bank and see which of you can skip a rock the farthest before you head back.

title: Berry Picking at the Orchard
description: Spend a morning at a local orchard or farm filling baskets with whatever's ripe, then argue on the drive home about what you're going to bake with it.

title: Birding With a Guide
description: Join a guided nature walk built around spotting local birds, and let someone who knows the calls point out everything you'd have walked straight past.

title: Drone Over a Hidden Lake
description: Hike out to a hidden alpine lake with a drone in your pack and capture the whole view from above. Check the rules for the area before you launch.

title: Wildflowers at Peak Bloom
description: Time your hike for peak wildflower season, then walk it slowly and count how many different varieties the two of you can spot in bloom.

title: Beat the Sun to the Top
How Many Waterfalls in One Day
description: Plan a route that strings together as many waterfalls as you can reach on foot in a day, then keep a running count until your legs call it.

title: Arch From Every Angle
description: Hike out to a natural arch or an oddly shaped rock formation, then circle the whole thing and study it from every angle until you find the best view.

title: Splash Break on the Trail
description: Hike until you hit a river or a creek, then stop and cool off properly, kicking water at each other before you carry on down the trail.

title: Climb, Then Picnic
description: Get on the wall for an afternoon, indoors or out, then unpack a picnic at the base once your forearms have officially given up on you.

title: Rappelling, Rope in Hand
description: Pick your drop: off the Cedars (scope out the cameras first), Falls Creek Falls with a swimsuit and a dry rope, or the bridge in Spencer, Idaho.

title: Zip the Provo Canyon
description: Strap into a harness and fly across Provo Canyon on a zip line, with just enough time between platforms to look down and regret looking down.

title: Axe Throwing Tournament
description: Book a lane, run an actual bracket between the two of you, and bring your own food so neither of you has to stop for dinner afterward.

title: Bomb the Canyon on a Longboard
Clue Race Through Downtown
description: Race each other through city streets solving a clue at every checkpoint, with the finish line staying hidden until one of you cracks the last one.

title: Silent Disco on Wheels
description: Join a guided bike ride where everyone wears wireless headphones playing the same curated playlist, so you're dancing on your pedals while the street stays silent.

title: Build Your Own Boot Camp
description: Take a boot camp fitness class together, or skip the gym and design your own circuit at the park, pushing each other through every round of it.

title: Capoeira, Then Brazilian Food
description: Take a capoeira class and try to keep up with the footwork, then head straight to a Brazilian restaurant to replace everything you just burned off.

title: Up in a Balloon
description: Book a hot air balloon ride and drift over everything while the light is still soft. Dress up and add a formal dinner if you want a real occasion.

title: Jump Out of a Plane
description: Book tandem jumps so neither of you has to do this alone, then spend the rest of the day telling anyone who'll listen that you went through with it.

title: Speed Record on the Wall
description: Pick one route at the climbing gym, run it until you both have it dialed, then put a stopwatch on it and race for the fastest clean time.

title: Bungee Off the Bridge
description: Step off a bridge or a platform on a bungee cord and fall until the rope decides to catch you. The hardest part is the two seconds beforehand.

title: Dune Buggy Desert Run
description: Take a dune buggy tour across desert terrain and spend an hour getting sandblasted, bounced around, and grinning the entire way through it.

title: Raft the Class III Rapids
description: Get in a raft with a guide and take on Class III water together, paddling hard through the big stuff and holding on through everything after.

title: Paddleboard the River Waves
description: Take a stand-up paddle board onto moving river water with real waves in it, and see which of you can stay standing the longest.

title: Canyoneering Down the Falls
description: Work your way down a canyon, rappelling over waterfalls as you go, with cold water running past you for most of the descent.

title: Steep Trail, Downhill Only
description: Find a steep downhill mountain bike trail, get a ride to the top, and let gravity handle the rest of the afternoon for you.

title: Step Off a Mountain Ridge
description: Run off a ridge under a paraglider and ride the air back down, with the whole valley spread out somewhere underneath your feet.

title: Ice Axes and Frozen Falls
description: Strap on crampons, take up ice axes, and climb a frozen waterfall one swing at a time. Go with a guide the first time you try it.

title: Real Rock, Real Rope
description: Trade the climbing gym for an actual cliff, with proper gear and someone experienced holding the other end of the rope. Real rock feels nothing like plastic.

title: Kayak Class, Then the River
description: Take a whitewater kayaking class in the morning, then put everything you just learned to work running the real river that same afternoon.

title: Squeeze Through the Tight Stuff
description: Go deep into a cave system with technical passages, crawling and squeezing through gaps where nothing but your headlamp gets there ahead of you.

title: Speed Skate the Long Hill
description: Lace up inline skates at the top of a long hill and let it rip. Pads are strongly recommended, and stopping is entirely your own problem.

title: Wakeboard Trick Attempts
description: Take turns behind the boat working on tricks, and count how many either of you lands before the lake wins and you call it a day.

title: Learn to Throw a Punch
description: Take a class together in kickboxing, boxing, or judo, and find out which of you is secretly dangerous after twenty minutes of instruction.

title: Snowboarding on Dirt
description: Strap into a mountain board and ride it down a dirt slope. It's snowboarding without the snow, and the landings are noticeably less forgiving.

title: Slackline Balance Battle
description: String a slackline between two trees and challenge each other to cross it. Expect a lot of falling before either of you manages three steps.

title: Freefall, If You Dare
description: Go BASE jumping if it's legally available where you are, or book a skydive with a long freefall instead. Either way, the ground arrives quickly.

title: Get Certified, Dive a Reef
description: Take a scuba certification course together, then put the card straight to use on a reef dive. That first breath underwater is the part you'll remember.

title: Massive Dunes, One Board
description: Climb a big sand dune, point your board downhill, and ride it out. The climb back up is the workout nobody bothers to warn you about.

title: Rock Hop Race
description: Find a stretch of river thick with stepping stones and race each other across without touching water. Soaked shoes mean you lost that round.

title: Peak Bagging Against the Clock
description: Pick a demanding peak, start a timer at the trailhead, and push hard all the way to the top. Write down your time and try to beat it next month.

title: Canoe the Whitewater
description: Take a canoe into moving whitewater for a proper expedition, where paddling in sync with each other stops being optional very quickly.

title: Real Boulders, No Ropes
description: Find outdoor boulder problems on natural rock, haul a crash pad out with you, and take turns spotting each other through the hard moves.

title: Parkour for Beginners
description: Take an intro parkour class and learn to vault, roll, and land without hurting yourselves. Every wall in the city looks different afterward.

title: Raft the Narrow Canyon
description: Run a raft through a canyon so tight you could nearly touch both walls, letting the current push you through the narrow passages.

title: Multi-Pitch Climbing Course
description: Sign up for an advanced multi-pitch course and learn to climb a long route in stages, swapping leads and belaying each other the whole way up.

title: Crawl Spaces and Cave Mud
description: Go caving somewhere with genuinely technical passages, crawling on your bellies through gaps and coming out the other side covered in mud.

title: Luge Track, Face First
description: Book a session on an iced luge or skeleton track and fly down it on your back or headfirst. Terrifying, and mercifully over in seconds.

title: Summit Expedition
description: Take on a real mountaineering objective together, with an alpine start, a long climb, and a summit you'll both take full credit for later.

title: Free the Heel, Free the Mind
Hands and Feet to the Summit
Swim With Sharks in Idaho
description: Head to the East Idaho Aquarium and get in the water with the sharks. It runs $20 with a Glass Card, which is a bargain for the story alone.

title: Daybreak Park Zipline
description: Spend an afternoon at Daybreak park and take turns on the zipline there until one of you finally admits it's mostly built for kids.

title: Camp at Mutual Dale
description: Set up camp at the Mutual Dale spot in American Fork Canyon, close enough to town that forgetting something isn't fatal, far enough to feel away.

title: Let Fish Eat Your Feet
description: Head to Layton Mall and try the fish spa, where tiny fish nibble the dead skin off your feet while you both try very hard not to flinch.

title: Crash a Wedding at Thanksgiving Point
description: Wander the grounds at Thanksgiving Point and, if you're feeling bold, edge into a wedding reception long enough to grab a piece of cake and one dance.

title: Fighter Jets in Roy
description: Spend a couple of hours among the aircraft at Hill Air Force Base in Roy, where everything is louder-looking and far bigger up close than you expect.

title: Ducks at Highland Glen
description: Take something duck-friendly to Highland Glen Park in Lehi and spend an easy afternoon by the water feeding them and deciding which one runs the place.

title: The Soap Factory on Center
description: Stop by the soap factory off Center Street and browse until you've each found a scent you can't stop smelling the whole drive home.

title: Five-Dollar Mini Golf
description: Play a round of $5 miniature golf at the mouth of Provo Canyon, where the stakes are low and the loser covers whatever you do next.

title: Dueling Pianos at Keys on Main
Tuesday Jazz at the Gallivan
description: Catch the Tuesday night jazz at the Gallivan Center, where you can sit close, talk between sets, and let a live band carry the evening.

title: Wander the Peace Gardens
description: Take a slow loop through the Peace Gardens in Salt Lake City, where every corner opens onto something new and nobody out there is in a hurry.

title: Creamery Cones in the Park
description: Grab something from the BYU Creamery and take it to the park right beside it, where you can sit, eat fast before it melts, and watch the evening go.

title: I Spy the Roots of Knowledge
description: Stand in front of the Roots of Knowledge windows at UVU and play I Spy, taking turns picking details out of the glass until your necks give out.

title: Old Ephraim's Grave, Legend Included
description: Make the trip out to Old Ephraim's Grave and bring the Legend along to read aloud once you're standing there. It lands differently at the spot.

title: Bees Game, Cheap Seats
description: Catch an SLC Bees game from the cheap rows, split a hot dog, and pay roughly half your attention to the baseball happening down there.

title: Grizzlies Hockey Night
description: Get tickets to an SLC Grizzlies game and spend the night yelling at the ice along with everyone else in the building.

title: Rent Bikes, Ride Salt Lake
description: Grab a pair of rental bikes and ride around Salt Lake with no fixed route, stopping at whatever looks worth stopping for along the way.

title: Temple Visitor's Center Stop
description: Walk through the Visitor's Center at the temple together, take your time with the exhibits, and sit for a while in the quiet before heading back out.

title: Capitol Steps and Legislature
description: Tour the State Capitol and sit in on the Legislature if they happen to be in session. The building is worth the trip and the debates are free.

title: Bear Lake Turquoise Swim
description: Make the drive out to Bear Lake and get straight into that turquoise water. Pack lunch ahead of time, because you won't want to leave to find any.

title: Hike Among the Goblins
description: Visit Goblin Valley and wander the hoodoos, ducking between rock shapes that look like they were carved by someone with a real sense of humor.

title: Out to the Spiral Jetty
description: Drive to the Spiral Jetty on the north shore of the Great Salt Lake and walk the coil all the way to its center. Long trip for art, worth it.

title: Sunset at Dead Horse Point
description: Get to Dead Horse Point in time for sunset and watch the light drop across the canyons below. Bring a jacket, because it cools off fast up there.

title: Picnic Near Sundance
description: Drive up to the Sundance Mountain Resort area, find a spot with a view, and eat lunch surrounded by more mountain than you know what to do with.

title: Kayak Strawberry Reservoir
description: Bring kayaks out to Strawberry Reservoir and paddle with mountains on every side. Go early, when the water is still glassy and nobody else is out.

title: Dinosaur Tracks at Mill Canyon
description: Head to the dinosaur tracks at Mill Canyon near Moab and put your hands in prints left by something enormous a very long time ago.

title: Every Overlook on Byway 12
description: Drive Scenic Byway 12 with one rule between you: stop at every single scenic overlook, no matter how many there are or how late it gets.

title: Natural Bridges Near Monticello
description: Make the drive to the natural bridges near Monticello and walk beneath spans of rock that water spent a few million years quietly carving out.

title: Photo Shoot on the Salt Flats
description: Drive out to the Bonneville Salt Flats and take photos across that endless white expanse, where there's nothing in the frame but the two of you.

title: Spires of Kodachrome Basin
description: Visit Kodachrome Basin State Park and hike among the stone spires, which look less like rocks and more like something deliberately set there.

title: Cabin Weekend at Fish Lake
description: Drive out to Fish Lake, rent a cabin for the weekend, and spend two full days doing very little on purpose and with no apologies.

title: Petrified Wood Hunt
description: Explore the petrified wood areas near Escalante and find pieces of an ancient forest turned to stone, with the grain still showing in the rock.

title: Hobble Creek Hike and Lunch
description: Head up Hobble Creek Canyon for an easy scenic hike, then stop somewhere green along the way to eat whatever lunch you packed for it.

title: Newspaper Rock Petroglyphs
description: Stop at Newspaper Rock near Moab and stand in front of a wall covered in petroglyphs, guessing out loud at what each one was meant to say.

title: Buffalo on Antelope Island
description: Drive out to Antelope Island and go looking for the buffalo herds. Stay in the car when they're close, and bring a camera with some zoom on it.

title: Wait for Crystal Geyser
description: Visit the Crystal Geyser near Green River and see if you catch it going off. If it doesn't, the river and the rock make the trip worth it anyway.

title: Red Rock Swimming at Sand Hollow
description: Spend the day at Sand Hollow State Park swimming in water ringed by red rock, with easy hiking on hand whenever you need to dry off.

title: Soak at Mystic Hot Springs
description: Drive to the Mystic Hot Springs near Monroe and settle into the warm water together for a long soak and an afternoon with nothing else on it.

title: Quiet Day at Piute Reservoir
description: Drive out to Piute Reservoir with fishing gear and no agenda at all, and see how long the two of you can sit there without saying anything.

title: Red Canyon Near Panguitch
description: Take the drive out to the Red Canyon scenic area near Panguitch, where the rock turns a shade of orange your camera won't quite believe.

title: Overlooks at Huntington
description: Spend the day at Huntington State Park hiking out to the scenic overlooks, then argue about which one you'd come back for.

title: Three Peaks, One Hard Hike
description: Take on the challenging hike from the Three Peaks trailhead and find out how the two of you handle a real climb side by side.

title: Follow Cascade Springs
description: Drive to Cascade Springs and follow the natural waterways as they step down the hillside, stopping wherever the water sounds best.

title: Paddleboats at Bear Lake Marina
description: Rent a paddleboat at the Bear Lake Marina and pedal out onto the water together. It's more work and more fun than it looks from shore.

title: Paria Rimrocks Slot Canyons
description: Visit the Paria Rimrocks and explore the slot canyons out there, squeezing between walls that keep the sunlight out until the middle of the day.

title: Ghost Town at Grafton
description: Drive out to Grafton Ghost Town and walk the abandoned settlement, peering into buildings that people packed up and left a long time ago.

title: Backroad Hot Springs
description: Track down the natural hot springs near Monroe or Salina and spend an afternoon soaking somewhere most people drive straight past without noticing.

title: Raft the Green, Camp the Bank
description: Head to Green River for a day of rafting, then set up camp right on the riverside and fall asleep to the sound of the water moving past.

title: Camp and Cast at Bear Lake
Capitol Lawn Picnic
description: Pack a lunch and take it to the park by the Capitol, where the grass is good and the building makes an absurdly grand backdrop for a sandwich.

title: Lawn Games Behind the Capitol
description: Bring whatever games pack flat, cards or frisbee or bocce, and set up on the grass behind the Capitol for a lazy but competitive afternoon.

title: Picnic on Center Street
description: Grab food and claim a bench or a patch of grass at the park on Center Street, close enough to everything that you can restock mid-picnic.

title: Pedal There, Picnic Here
description: Strap a picnic to your bikes, ride to the park by the longest route you can find, and eat all of it once you arrive. The ride home is harder.

title: Sweat It Out at the Park
description: Head to the park and play whatever gets you both moving, whether that's tag, frisbee, or soccer, until you're genuinely out of breath.

title: Ducks, Swings, Candlelight
description: Spend an evening at the park feeding the ducks, messing around on the playground equipment, and finishing with a candlelit picnic on the grass.

title: Deserted Island Picnic
description: Pack a lunch, find a wide grassy island in the middle of a road, and eat there while traffic rolls past on both sides of you.

title: Trail Lunch
description: Pick a trail and pack a real lunch or dinner instead of snacks, then find a spot along the way that's worth stopping to eat at.

title: Picnic in the Middle of the Mall
description: Spread a blanket somewhere in the mall, lay out actual picnic food, and eat it while shoppers walk past trying to work out what you're doing.

title: Willow Park Playground Rematch
description: Take over the playground at Willow Park and race each other across the equipment like you're both a third of your actual age.

title: Rate Every Swing in Town
description: Hit every park in the area, rank the swings and slides at each one, then head back to the winner and cook out there.

title: Hopscotch and Happy Meals
description: Spend an afternoon doing kid things on purpose: hopscotch on the sidewalk, a real go on the playground, and Happy Meals eaten on the curb.

title: First Light, First Breakfast
description: Get up early enough to beat everyone else to a mountain overlook, then eat breakfast up there while the valley below is still waking up.

title: Blanket Fort and Cloud Watching
description: Build a blanket fort out in the grass, lay a spread of snacks inside it, and spend the afternoon arguing about what the clouds look like.

title: Projector Movie in the Park
description: Haul a projector out to the park at dusk, aim it at a sheet or a blank wall, and watch a movie outside with whoever wanders over.

title: Park Hopping Scavenger Hunt
description: Make a list of things to track down, like a specific tree, a sculpture, or a strange bench, then drive between parks checking them off.

title: Backyard Badminton Championship
description: Rig up a badminton net on the grass with whatever you've got on hand, then play a full tournament until one of you is officially champion.

title: Hammock, Two Trees, No Plans
description: Bring a hammock to the park, string it between two good trees, and spend the whole afternoon taking turns doing absolutely nothing in it.

title: The One-Letter Picnic
description: Pick a letter, then build an entire picnic out of foods that start with it. The grocery run is half the fun and most of the arguing.

title: Dirt Sculpture Masterpiece
description: Find a sandbox or a patch of dirt at the park and build the most elaborate thing the two of you can manage before somebody's kid levels it.

title: Dessert First, Obviously
description: Run a picnic entirely backwards: dessert first, then lunch, then snacks at the end. It makes no sense at all and feels great.

title: Chalk Takeover
description: Bring a bucket of sidewalk chalk to the park and cover the pavement with art the two of you know will be gone by the next rain.

title: Cardboard Box Fort Picnic
description: Find a giant cardboard box, turn it into a fort at the park, and eat your entire picnic sitting inside it like a couple of kids.

title: Golden Hour at the Park
description: Get to the park right as the light turns gold, then shoot photos of each other with nothing but trees and open sky behind you.

title: Cooler Full of Water Balloons
description: Fill a cooler with water balloons instead of drinks, eat your picnic first, then use every single balloon in that cooler on each other.

title: The Ridiculously Fancy Picnic
description: Do a picnic properly for once: real dishes, cloth napkins, and battery-powered candles on the blanket. Overdressing for it is strongly encouraged.

title: Busking Picnic
description: Bring instruments, or just a speaker, to the park and play a set for whoever happens to walk past while the two of you eat.

title: Nature Bingo Over Lunch
description: Make bingo cards full of birds and plants you might spot, then play them while you picnic. First to a full row gets the last cookie.

title: One Canvas, Two Painters
description: Bring a big canvas to the park and work on it together between bites, with neither of you allowed to claim a side as your own.

title: Read Aloud Between Bites
description: Each bring a book you love, then take turns reading passages out loud to each other over a picnic. Snacks and chapters, alternating.

title: The Park You've Never Tried
description: Pick a park neither of you has been to, walk the entire thing, and sketch a rough map of its best features before you leave.

title: Eat Only What You Find
description: Set a rule that nothing store-bought lands on the blanket, then find out what the two of you can actually forage or gather for lunch.

title: Telescope After the Sunset
description: Bring a telescope and dinner, eat while the sun goes down, and stay out to find whatever the sky offers once it's completely dark.

title: Rate Every Spot in the Park
description: Move your blanket to a new spot every twenty minutes and score each one on shade, view, and grass quality until you crown a winner.

title: Tent Life at the Park
description: Pitch a two-person tent right there at the park, lay a picnic out in front of it, and pretend you camped somewhere far more remote.

title: Write the Park a Song
description: Bring a ukulele or a guitar to your picnic and write a song about the park you're sitting in, with at least one verse about the ducks.

title: Taste Test Showdown
description: Pick one food and buy several versions of it, then run a blind taste test on the picnic blanket to settle which one actually wins.

title: Picnic in a Kiddie Pool
description: Fill a kiddie pool out on the grass, climb in with your feet under the water, and eat your entire picnic without once getting out.

title: Letters to Your Future Selves
description: Bring a journal to your picnic and write letters to the two of you a year from now, then seal them and pick a date to open them.

title: Obstacle Course Between Courses
description: Build an obstacle course across the park and race it between picnic courses, so dessert only gets served once somebody clears the last one.

title: Picnic High, Roll Down
description: Haul your picnic to the top of the biggest hill you can find, eat all of it up there, then roll the entire way back down.

title: Pose With the Statues
description: Bring a camera and work your way around the park staging increasingly ridiculous photos with every statue, fountain, and sign you come across.

title: The Progressive Picnic
description: Move to a new spot every fifteen minutes and serve one course at each stop, so the picnic crosses the whole park before dessert lands.

title: Picnic by String Light
description: Head out at dusk with string lights, lanterns, and glow sticks as your only light, then eat by the glow once the sun is fully gone.

title: Storyboard It, Then Act It Out
Board Games at the Picnic Table
Disc Golf at UVU
description: Grab a set of discs and play a round of frisbee golf, whether that's the UVU course or anywhere else nearby with baskets and a bit of elevation.

title: Two Wheels, One Route
description: Pick a route, mountain or road, and ride it together. The only rule is that whoever chooses the hills has to lead the way up them.

title: Rack 'Em Up
description: Find a pool table, run your own best-of-seven tournament, and agree beforehand on exactly what the loser owes the winner.

title: Build a Marble Track
description: Build a marble track out of cardboard, tape, and whatever else is lying around the house, then race marbles down it until you've crowned a champion.
Make it a rule that you play a different disc golf course every single time, and work your way through every one you can drive to.

title: Skates On All Night
description: Go roller skating or rollerblading together, or commit properly and keep the skates on everywhere you go for the rest of the night.

title: Glow Tennis After Dark
description: Play tennis at night with a fluorescent ball and a glow-string net, where you mostly track a streak of light and swing hopefully at it.

title: Wrong Ball, Right Game
description: Play soccer with a football, or football with a tennis ball, or anything else that shouldn't work. The rules stay the same; the equipment does not.

title: Invent a Sport
description: Make up an entirely new sport from scratch, write the rules down properly, then play it seriously enough that one of you wins the first championship.

title: Buckets at the Driving Range
description: Split a bucket of balls at the driving range and swing away, with no scorecard and nobody watching your form except each other.

title: The Great Valley Race
description: Plan a road rally with stops all around the valley, where the clue waiting at each one points you to the next. First to finish picks dinner.

title: GPS Treasure Course
description: Set up a GPS course across campus with coordinates leading from one point to the next, and stash something worth finding at the very end.

title: Somebody Hid It, You Find It
Try Everything in the Store
description: Wander a sporting goods store testing every piece of gear you can get your hands on, from the treadmills to the kayaks to the massage chairs.

title: Twister, Harder Rules
description: Play a round of Twister, then start swapping in sillier body parts on every spin until neither of you can reach anything without collapsing.

title: Duck Duck Goose, Grown-Up Edition
description: Round up a few people and play the games you grew up with: Duck Duck Goose, tag, Red Rover. They hold up far better than you'd expect.

title: Jump Rope Olympics
description: Spend an evening with a jump rope running follow-the-leader, rope tag, and speed and endurance contests until your calves formally object.

title: The One-Dollar Egg Drop
description: Give yourselves $1 each to build a protective package for an egg, then drop them from somewhere high and see whose egg walks away intact.

title: Obstacle Course Olympics
description: Build an obstacle course or invent a set of ridiculous events, then compete through all of them and hand out an actual medal at the end.

title: UNO in the Mall
description: Sit down right in the middle of the mall and play a full game of UNO on the floor while shoppers walk around the two of you.

title: Board Game Table Rotation
description: Put a different board game on each table, Scrabble and Balderdash and whatever else you own, split into teams, and rotate until all of them are played.

title: Six on Six, Then Cocoa
description: Get six guys and six girls together for a real game of basketball or touch football, then pile inside afterward for hot chocolate.

title: Mud Football, Lake Rinse
description: Play a full game of football in the mud, get completely filthy doing it, then swim in the lake until you're clean enough to drive home.

title: Knee Football Tackle Rules
description: Play tackle football with one rule: everyone stays on their knees the entire game. Slower, dumber, and considerably more painful than it sounds.

title: Nosebleeds at the Basketball Game
description: Get tickets to a basketball game, sit wherever's cheap, and spend as much attention on the crowd and the halftime bit as the actual game.

title: Bracket Night at the Pool Table
Cornhole in the Sand
description: Set cornhole boards up on the beach or any patch of sand and play until the tide, the sun, or your throwing arms make you stop.

title: Borrow a Backyard, Play Badminton
description: Take over someone's backyard for a badminton tournament, invite enough people for real rounds, and keep score on whatever paper you can find.

title: An Evening at the Climbing Gym
description: Head to an indoor climbing gym, rent the shoes, and work your way up the color-coded routes together until your grip finally gives out.

title: Rent, Paddle, Explore
description: Rent kayaks or paddleboards and spend a few hours on whatever water is closest, poking into every inlet and shoreline you come across.

title: Crabwalk Relay Races
description: Run a relay tournament where every leg has to be covered a stupid way: backwards, hopping, crabwalking. Falling over costs you the lead.

title: Beach Ball Kickball
description: Play a full game of kickball with an oversized beach ball, which floats, curves, and makes every single kick completely unpredictable.

title: Batting Cage Power Contest
description: Split a round of tokens at the batting cage and find out which of you can make the loudest, hardest contact before your hands start stinging.

title: Chalk Court Tournament
description: Draw the games straight onto the pavement, Twister and hopscotch and four square, then play a full tournament across every one of them.

title: Four Square Comeback
description: Find a wall or a patch of pavement and play four square or wall ball, where the rules are whatever the person in the top square says.

title: Three-Legged Race Trials
description: Tie your ankles together and race, then keep running heats until the two of you finally figure out how to move like one person.

title: Lawn Bowling by Dusk
description: Set up a lawn bowling game on a flat stretch of grass and play into the evening, when the fading light makes every roll harder to judge.

title: No Rope, Just Rock
description: Head to an outdoor bouldering spot and climb close to the ground without a rope, spotting each other through the moves that matter.

title: Spikeball in the Park
description: Set up a spikeball net at the park and play roundnet until you're both diving into the grass after shots you should have let go.

title: Beach Ball Soccer
description: Play a soccer game with an oversized beach ball, where every kick sends it somewhere unintended and defending is completely hopeless.

title: Trampoline Park Freestyle
description: Book an hour at a trampoline park and spend it flipping, bouncing off the walls, and landing in the foam pit until your legs quit on you.

title: Toss, Clank, Repeat
description: Set up ladder toss or horseshoes in the yard and play the kind of long, slow, chatty game where nobody's really tracking the score.

title: The Backyard Games
description: Invent five or six ridiculous sports, run them all in a single afternoon as your own Olympics, and keep a medal table with real standings.

title: Sack Race Across the Terrain
description: Race in sacks across grass, sand, gravel, and any other surface you can find, then decide which one wrecked the two of you fastest.

title: Knockout, Loser Dances
description: Play knockout at a basketball court with one extra rule: whoever gets knocked out has to perform a silly dance before rejoining the line.

title: Stone Skipping Distance Record
description: Find a flat stretch of water, hunt down the best skipping stones, and compete purely on distance until one of you sets a record that stands.

title: Hula Hoop Endurance Test
description: See which of you can keep a hula hoop going the longest, or just teach each other until you can both manage more than four rotations.

title: Bike Course You Built
description: Set up an obstacle course with cones, ramps, and whatever else you can find, then ride it on bikes and time each other's runs through it.

title: H-O-R-S-E With Trick Shots
description: Play H-O-R-S-E at a basketball court where every attempt has to be a trick shot: backwards, one-handed, off the fence, whatever you dream up.

title: Cannonball Scoring System
description: Head to a pool and hold a diving and cannonball competition, scoring each other out of ten on height, form, and sheer splash volume.

title: Stilt Walking Relay
description: Get a pair of stilts, learn to walk on them without falling over, then race each other in relay legs back and forth across the yard.

title: Water Balloon Volleyball
description: Play volleyball over a net with water balloons instead of a ball, catching them in towels and launching them back before they burst.

title: Driving Range House Rules
description: Head to the driving range and invent your own game with point multipliers for distance, accuracy, and anything else you feel like rewarding.

title: Double Dutch Duel
description: Run a jump rope battle through every format you can manage, from singles to couples to team styles, until somebody's legs give out.

title: Neighborhood Scavenger Sprint
description: Write a list of things to find or photograph around the neighborhood, then race each other to see who can finish the whole list first.

title: Badminton in Golden Light
description: Schedule a badminton match for sunrise or sunset, when the light is gorgeous and the air is still. The warm glow makes a casual game feel like something more.

title: Beat the Clock, Not Each Other
Happy Little Accidents
description: Follow a Bob Ross episode and paint along with him in real time, then raise the stakes by trying the next one blindfolded or at triple speed.

title: Repaint a Thrift Store Canvas
description: Pick up a couple of old paintings from DI and paint something entirely new right over the top of them. No great art was harmed here.

title: Block of Ice, Sharp Tools
description: Get a couple of ice blocks and carve them into something recognizable before they melt out from under you. Work fast and keep your fingers clear.

title: Melted Crayon Art
description: Glue crayons along the top of a canvas, aim a hair dryer at them, and let the wax run down into something neither of you can fully control.

title: Finger Paint, Toe Paint
description: Get out the paint and go at a canvas with your fingers, then switch to your toes once that stops being difficult. Dinner comes after the cleanup.

title: Free Portraits, Mall Edition
description: Set up two easels in the mall offering free portraits: one of you does real work, the other draws stick figures. Let a stranger pick the winner.

title: Artists for One Night
description: Buy cheap canvases and a few tubes of paint, clear the table, and spend an entire evening making art neither of you is remotely qualified to make.

title: Tie-Dyed Purses
description: Sew or assemble a couple of simple purses together, then tie-dye them in whatever color scheme you can both agree on. No two come out alike.

title: Build a Wooden Puzzle
description: Design a puzzle on paper, cut it out of wood, then hand them to each other and see which of you solves the other's first.

title: Launch a Tiny Hot Air Balloon
description: Build a small hot air balloon out of light material, get the air inside it hot, and watch it lift off. Launch it somewhere open and safe.

title: Clothespin Furniture Workshop
description: Make something small and genuinely useful out of household bits, like a pot holder or a napkin holder built from clothespins, then put it to work.

title: Sandals From Old Tires
description: Cut soles from an old tire and rig straps out of webbing or leather to build your own sandals, then walk around the block testing your work.

title: Salvage Yard Sculpture
description: Pick up scrap metal from a salvage yard and build something out of it together. Wear gloves, and let the ugliest piece be the centerpiece.

title: Spray Paint Your Own Tag
description: Grab a sheet of plywood and a few cans of spray paint, then teach yourselves to lay down a graffiti tag without ruining the whole board.

title: Calligraphy, Burnt Edges
description: Write poems for each other, copy them out in calligraphy, singe the paper edges for effect, and trade them at the end of the night.

title: Crayons and Coloring Books
description: Break out crayons and children's coloring books, or cut valentines out of construction paper regardless of what month it happens to be.

title: Toe Painting Party
description: Invite people over, hand out paint, and make everyone paint using their toes. Dinner comes after the cleanup, which will take a while.

title: One Roll of Film
description: Load up a film camera, shoot a single roll between the two of you, and wait on the developing to see what you actually captured.

title: Photo Contest, Prints Traded
description: Spend the day shooting photos, print your best ones, and swap them at the end so you each go home with the other's favorite shot.

title: Tourists in Your Own Town
description: Buy disposable cameras and spend the day photographing your own town like you've never seen it before. No deleting and no do-overs.

title: Build a Longboard, Ride It
description: Shape and finish your own longboard decks, mount the trucks, then take them outside and find out whose build actually rolls better.

title: Whittle a Walking Stick
description: Find a good solid stick, take a knife to it, and whittle a walking stick worth keeping. Slow work, good conversation, mind your thumbs.

title: Rescue an Old Piece
description: Find a beat-up piece of furniture or an antique and spend a day sanding, repairing, and refinishing it back into something you'd actually use.

title: Get Your Hands Dirty
description: Plant flowers or start a small garden together, choosing things that will need both of you to come back and keep watering them.

title: Flower Arranging Face-Off
description: Buy an armful of flowers, split them evenly, and each build an arrangement at home. Then argue about whose one earns the kitchen table.

title: Button Maker Mayhem
description: Get hold of a button maker and turn inside jokes, bad photos, and terrible slogans into pins the two of you will actually wear.

title: Draw Your Own Comic
description: Write and draw a comic strip together, one of you on words and the other on pictures, then swap roles halfway through the story.

title: Bookmarks With Pressed Flowers
description: Make bookmarks out of card and decorate them with flowers you pressed yourselves, then put them straight into the books you're each reading.

title: Build a Birdhouse
description: Build a birdhouse or some other small wooden thing from scratch, then paint it badly and hang it somewhere you'll both see it often.

title: Pour Your Own Candles
description: Melt the wax, pick your scents and colors, and pour a batch of candles together. Label them with names only the two of you understand.

title: One Giant Sheet of Paper
description: Tape an enormous sheet of paper to the wall or the floor and fill it together, with neither of you allowed to plan what comes next.

title: Broken Tile Mosaic
description: Smash up old tiles or save your eggshells, then set the pieces into a mosaic. It's messy, slow, and surprisingly good for talking.

title: Iron-On Shirt Designs
description: Design something ridiculous, print it as an iron-on transfer, and press it onto shirts you'll then have to be brave enough to wear out.

title: Frames From Sticks and Driftwood
description: Build picture frames out of popsicle sticks or driftwood you collected yourselves, then fill them with photos of the two of you.

title: Magazine Cutout Collage
description: Tear apart a stack of old magazines and build a mixed-media collage together, adding paint wherever the paper runs out on you.

title: Soap From Scratch
description: Make soap from scratch together, choosing your own scents and colors, then wait out the cure time before either of you gets to use it.

title: Invent a Board Game
description: Design a board game from nothing at all: rules, board, pieces, the lot. Then play it and immediately start arguing about the balance.

title: Paint It, They Fire It
description: Pick your pieces at a paint-and-fire studio, decorate them however you like, and come back a week later to see how they turned out.

title: Beads, Thread, and Patience
description: Spend an evening making bracelets or beaded jewelry for each other, on the condition that you both have to wear whatever the other makes.

title: Vision Board for Two
description: Cut out images and words for the life you want and build a vision board together, then hang it somewhere you'll both walk past every day.

title: Build a Tiny World
description: Layer soil and moss into a glass container, add small plants and whatever decorations amuse you, and build a tiny world for the shelf.

title: Decoupage Everything
description: Glue paper cutouts onto plates or boxes and seal them, turning plain objects into things covered in whatever images the two of you like.

title: Design Your Own Deck
description: Design and print a custom deck of playing cards or tarot cards, with the two of you turning up on at least a few of them.

title: Scrapbook the Good Parts
description: Print your favorite photos and build a scrapbook of everything you've done together so far, captions and ticket stubs and all.

title: Pressed Petals on Paper
description: Press leaves and flowers flat, then arrange them into framed art on paper. It takes a few days of waiting and one good afternoon.

title: Pour Concrete Planters
description: Mix concrete, pour it into molds, and cast your own planters or decorative pieces. The rough edges are half of the charm.

title: Diorama in a Shadow Box
description: Build a tiny scene inside a shadow box, piece by careful piece, and make it somewhere the two of you would genuinely want to visit.

title: Make Next Year's Calendar
description: Build a calendar or planner together using your own photos, inside jokes, and every date neither of you can afford to forget.

title: Knot Some Macramé
description: Learn a few macramé knots and make a wall hanging or a plant hanger. The first one will look homemade, which is entirely the point.

title: Origami Until It Works
description: Fold origami together until one of you produces something actually recognizable, then line the whole collection up on a shelf.

title: The Quilt You Finish Eventually
description: Start a quilt or patchwork blanket together and chip away at it over weeks. It ends up being a record of every evening you spent on it.

title: Nails, String, and Patience
description: Hammer nails into a board in a pattern, then wrap colored string between them until a shape appears out of all that chaos.

title: Make Paper From Scraps
description: Pulp old paper, press it into sheets, and dry them out into paper of your own, then write each other a note on the very first one.

title: Stickers of Your Own Design
description: Draw or design a batch of stickers, send them off to be printed, and then stick them on everything either of you owns.

title: Move a Photo to Canvas
description: Transfer a favorite photo onto canvas with gel medium, peel the paper back, and end up with something better than the print you started with.

title: Clay Figures, Fired in a Pit
A Fairy Garden in a Box
Tilt the Canvas, Let It Run
A Puzzle of Your Own Photo
Two-Foot Volcano Eruption
description: Build a volcano two to four feet tall out of whatever you can find, then set it off outside and stand well back when it finally goes.

title: Backyard Drive-In
description: Rig up a screen and a projector at someone's house, park the cars facing it, and run a proper drive-in movie night from the front seats.

title: Make Fire With a Bow Drill
description: Carve a bow drill and work at it until you get an ember, then coax that ember into an actual fire. It takes far longer than you'd think.

title: The Fake Country DMV
description: Invent a country, write its driving rules, make Photoshopped licenses, then take the whole bit somewhere small like Clarkston and see who plays along.

title: Invent a Geography Game
description: Design a world geography game from scratch, with your own rules and your own cards, then play it until one of you learns where everything is.

title: Piñata Party, Invite Everyone
description: Make a piñata from scratch, then build an entire party around swinging at it: blindfolds, a stick, and more candy than seems sensible.

title: Build a Bench Together
description: Cut, sand, and assemble a wooden bench for the yard or the porch, then sit on it together and find out whether it holds the two of you.

title: Raised Bed, Real Vegetables
description: Build a raised garden bed from scratch, fill it with good soil, and plant vegetables you'll actually want to eat once the season comes.

title: Pallet Wood Bookshelf
description: Break down pallets or reclaimed boards and build a bookshelf out of them, then fill it with the books you both keep leaving on the floor.

title: A Whole Birdhouse Village
description: Build several birdhouses instead of just one, decorate each of them differently, and hang them close enough together to call it a village.

title: Build a Bridge Over the Creek
description: Build a small footbridge across a creek or stream, and make it sturdy enough that you both trust it on the very first crossing.

title: Sandbox With Built-In Benches
description: Build a sandbox with seating around the edges, so there's somewhere to sit and supervise while the other one builds the castle.

title: Indoor Mini Golf Build
description: Turn a garage or basement into a miniature golf course with homemade obstacles, then play the whole thing and rank every hole you built.

title: Hooks, Racks, and Shelves
description: Pick one small wooden project the house actually needs, a towel rack or coat hooks or a shelf, and build it together in an afternoon.

title: Furniture for the Pet
description: Build a dog bed or another piece of pet furniture from scratch, then watch the animal ignore it entirely for the first three days.

title: A Mailbox Worth Noticing
description: Build and decorate a mailbox or a house address sign together, then put it up out front where everyone driving past will see it.

title: Build the Patio Set
description: Take on a real build together: a wooden deck or a full patio furniture set, finished over a weekend and used every summer after that.

title: A Catapult That Actually Works
description: Build a working catapult out of wood and tension, then spend the rest of the afternoon launching things across the yard at targets.

title: Build a Wooden Trunk
description: Build a storage chest or trunk out of wood, then fill it with all the stuff neither of you currently has anywhere else to put.

title: Treehouse, With Permission
description: Build a treehouse or a raised platform in a tree, with the owner's blessing secured first, then haul snacks up and stay a while.

title: A Sign With Your Initials
description: Make a sign for your room with your initials or a phrase that means something to the two of you, then hang it where visitors will read it.

title: Planter Boxes, Built to Fit
description: Build a set of wooden planter boxes sized for the garden you actually want, then fill them with soil and whatever you plan to grow.

title: Make Water Do the Work
description: Build a water wheel or water table that actually turns, then run water through it and keep adjusting until it spins the way you want.

title: Hidden Compartment Box
description: Build a wooden puzzle box with hidden compartments, then stash something small inside and see how long the other one takes to find it.

title: Cutting Board From Scratch
description: Glue, cut, and sand a wooden cutting board or serving platter, then oil it properly and put it to use for dinner that same night.

title: Tame the Spice Cupboard
description: Build a spice rack or kitchen organizer that fits your actual cupboard, then reorganize the entire shelf while you have it all out.

title: Jewelry Box With Real Drawers
description: Build a jewelry box with drawers and compartments that slide properly, which is considerably harder and more satisfying than it sounds.

title: Build a Carnival Game
description: Build a working carnival game, whether that's ring toss or a coin drop, then play it against each other for absurd homemade prizes.

title: A Case for the Keepsakes
description: Build a shadow box display case for the small things worth keeping, then fill it with the objects that still need explaining.

title: Charging Station, Handmade
description: Build a wooden phone stand or charging station for the entryway, so there's finally one agreed place where both your phones live.

title: Tiered Stand for the Plants
description: Build a plant stand or tiered shelf, then rearrange every plant you own onto it at least four times before you settle on an order.

title: Wall-Mounted Chalkboard Build
description: Build a whiteboard or chalkboard out of wood and paint, hang it somewhere central, and start leaving each other notes on it.

title: Bench That Opens Up
description: Build a wooden bench with a hinged lid so it doubles as storage, then argue cheerfully about what earns a place inside it.

title: Rig a Working Pulley
description: Rig up a working pulley system for no reason beyond the fact that you can, then use it to haul snacks and tools around the yard.

title: A Sealed Little Ecosystem
description: Layer stones, sand, soil, and live plants into a glass container and design a miniature landscape together, then keep it alive for years.

title: House Rules, Homemade Board
description: Invent the rules, draw the board on poster board, make pieces out of wood or clay, then playtest it with every silly rule you added.

title: Marble Run With Loops
description: Build a marble run from cardboard tubes, ramps, and buckets, then keep tweaking angles and heights until a marble finally makes it through.

title: Headboard Worth Waking Up To
description: Design and build a headboard from reclaimed wood or upholstered panels, or take on a whole bed frame. Real carpentry, and you sleep in the result.

title: A Rope Bridge in the Yard
description: String rope and wooden planks between two trees to build a bridge with handrails and footholds, then cross it and see how wobbly it really is.

title: Bottle Rack as Wall Art
description: Craft a beverage rack out of wood, copper pipe, or iron that holds bottles at odd angles and doubles as something worth looking at.

title: Scrap Wood, Geometric Wall
description: Gather colorful scrap wood, arrange the pieces into a geometric pattern on plywood, and glue them down. Sand and stain it to finish the piece.

title: Soap Box Derby Build
description: Build a gravity-powered soap box car out of wood and reclaimed parts, then race it down a sloped driveway and argue about the steering.

title: Gallery Wall, Frames and All
description: Build simple wooden frames in several sizes, fill them with your favorite photos, and hang the whole arrangement as one gallery wall.

title: Build an Outdoor Shower
description: Build a wooden enclosure with cedar slats or a privacy screen around an outdoor showerhead, and turn a corner of the yard into a small spa.

title: Suncatcher in the Window
description: Cut colored glass, join the pieces with copper foil, and solder the seams into a panel that throws color across the room all afternoon.

title: Hang a Swing From a Tree
description: Build a sturdy wooden swing seat, tie it to a strong branch with thick rope, then take turns testing it until you both trust the knots.

title: A Wall of Living Herbs
description: Build a wall-mounted planting system with pockets for herbs or succulents, then water it together and watch the wall slowly fill in.

title: Weatherproof Storage Bench
description: Build a waterproof wooden bench with a hinged seat that keeps cushions, garden tools, and outdoor clutter dry through the whole year.

title: Light Fixture, Your Design
description: Wrap fabric, paper, or wood strips around a frame for a lampshade, or build a geometric pendant from copper wire and glass. One room, transformed.

title: Stand for the Hammock
description: Build a sturdy A-frame stand for a hammock, cross-brace it properly, and test the load carefully before either of you lies down in it.

title: Paint the Kitchen Tiles
description: Paint your own designs onto plain ceramic tiles with food-safe glazes, then install them as a backsplash you'll look at every single day.

title: Escape Room on a Table
description: Design a miniature escape room with locks, hidden compartments, and riddles, then hand it to friends and enjoy watching them struggle.

title: Fire Pit and Benches
description: Build a fire pit enclosure with wooden benches around it, then spend every evening after that roasting s'mores in something you made.

title: Bookcase That Splits the Room
description: Build a tall freestanding bookcase that divides a room and stores everything, then fill it with books, plants, and whatever else fits.

title: Build a Ukulele, Play It
description: Build a working ukulele from wood blanks, add the strings and tuning pegs, then play a wobbly duet on the instrument you just made.

title: Tiny Houses, Tiny Bridges
description: Craft miniature wooden houses, fences, and bridges, then set them into a garden bed with moss and small plants to build a little world.

title: Pallet Couch, Real Cushions
description: Break down and sand wooden pallets, then build a couch or lounge set and add cushions. Cheap, rustic, and far more comfortable than expected.

title: Trebuchet Distance Trials
description: Build a working trebuchet, then spend the afternoon adjusting weight, angle, and release until it throws things a little farther each time.

title: Stepping Stones You Made
description: Press colored glass, tile shards, and stones into wet concrete to cast mosaic stepping stones for the garden path you walk every day.

title: Breakfast in Bed Tray
description: Build a lightweight lap desk or bed tray with folding legs, then put it to work for breakfast in bed the very next morning.

title: An Arch Worth Walking Through
description: Build a wooden arch or garden gate with lattice or carved detail, then plant something climbing that will cover it over the next few years.

title: Bury a Time Capsule
description: Build a sealed container, line it with fabric, and fill it with letters and mementos. Then pick a date years out to dig it up together.

title: Plants Hanging From Above
description: Build a rope-and-wood hanging system for potted plants, then spend the next few weeks rearranging which plant hangs where.

title: Guitars on the Wall
description: Build wall mounts that hold guitars or ukuleles safely and look good doing it, turning your instruments into part of the room's decor.

title: Sandbox With a Cooler
description: Build a sandbox with bench seating and a built-in cooler compartment, so the drinks stay cold while everyone else plays in the sand.

title: Baking With Grabber Arms
description: Bake something start to finish using nothing but extendo-arm grabber tools. Cracking a single egg becomes a genuine team achievement.

title: Blind Chocolate Bar Ranking
description: Buy ten chocolate bars, unwrap them out of sight, and taste-test blind to find out which of you can actually identify the most.

title: Sundae Off a Cliff
description: Build an ice cream sundae right at the edge of a cliff lookout, then eat the whole thing before the sun or the melting beats you to it.

title: Build a Baked Bear Sandwich
description: Head to Baked Bear and build your own ice cream sandwich from the cookie up, then try to eat the thing before it collapses on you.

title: Learn Someone Else's Recipe
description: Ask a friend, a parent, or a neighbor to teach you both the dish they're known for, then cook it together under their direct supervision.

title: Hot Dogs for Strangers
description: Make a batch of homemade hot dogs, then hand them out to people around town until you've run out of both buns and nerve.

title: Animal Desserts, Delivered
description: Make desserts shaped like 3D animals, box them up carefully, and deliver them to a rest home where they'll be genuinely appreciated.

title: Best Pizza Wins
description: Get a few couples together, hand out dough and toppings, and let a neutral party decide whose pizza actually came out best.

title: Mystery Pizza Delivery
description: Order delivery to a friend's house with no warning, watch them try to work out who sent it, then show up to pay and eat half of it.

title: One Course, Six Drive-Thrus
description: Eat one course at each of five or six fast food places, carrying a single straw the whole way. Dessert goes to whoever's still standing.

title: The Center Street Food Crawl
description: Work your way along Center Street and University, splitting one thing at every stop, until neither of you can face another bite.

title: Seed Spitting and Pie Throwing
description: Run a night of ridiculous food games: a LifeSaver-on-a-toothpick relay, cherry and watermelon seed spitting, and pie throwing to finish.

title: Dinner Served in Cookware
description: Serve the spaghetti straight from the pans, hand out spatulas instead of forks, and pour the drinks into vases. Presentation is not the point.

title: Tiny Food, Tiny Plates
description: Cook an entire dinner in miniature and serve it on the smallest plates you own. It tastes the same and looks a hundred times better.

title: Go Full Gourmet
description: Pick a genuinely ambitious recipe, split the prep between you, and cook a gourmet dinner that takes the whole evening and every pan you own.

title: Foil Packets on the Coals
description: Load foil packets with meat, potatoes, and vegetables, bury them in the coals, and dig them out when they're done. A cookout with no dishes.

title: Ice Cream Sculpting Contest
description: Everyone brings a half-gallon and a topping, then splits into groups to sculpt something out of ice cream before it melts. Best creation wins.

title: One Dollar Food Challenge
description: Give yourselves a dollar each and a silly food challenge to solve with it. A tight constraint does more for creativity than a full budget.

title: No Plates, Just Table
description: Scrub the kitchen table until it's spotless, then serve dinner straight onto it with nothing but forks. Strangely liberating, mildly unhinged.

title: One Dish, Five Fancy Names
description: Set a formal table and serve the same dish under a different name every course: macaroni and cheese, cheese with noodles, cheesy pasta, and onward.

title: Everything Starts With One Letter
description: Pick a letter and cook a whole meal where every ingredient starts with it. The shopping trip turns out to be the hardest part of the night.

title: Two Bowls, Two Ramens
description: Make ramen from scratch, then build each bowl completely differently and trade a few bites to work out whose toppings actually won.

title: Taco Truck Throwdown
description: See who can build the better taco, either from scratch at home or by hitting several taco trucks and ranking every single one you try.

title: Pasta Shapes, Taste Tested
